reception.text: The champagne arrangement drew no more than importers' notice; reciprocity proclamations were the small change of trade policy.

political_impact.text: France and Algeria gave American coffee, cacao, chocolate, vanilla and similar colonial foods, and American mineral oils, their lowest tariff rates in return for lower U.S. duties on sparkling wine.
political_impact.source: Additional Commercial Agreement, January 28, 1908, Foreign Relations of the United States, 1908

legacy.text: The arrangement ended on October 31, 1909, after twenty-one months; France asked for an extension and was told there was no constitutional way to grant one.
legacy.source: Payne-Aldrich Tariff Act, sec. 4, 36 Stat. 11; Knox notice of August 7, 1909

later_actions.text: The Payne-Aldrich Tariff Act replaced the Dingley reciprocity scheme and required six months' notice of termination, counted from April 30, 1909.
Secretary of State Knox notified France that its agreements of 1898, 1902 and 1908 would end on October 31, 1909.

political_impact.text: The proclamation cut 109,312 acres from the Lincoln National Forest, reducing it from 627,435 to 518,123 acres, and returned the land to the homestead laws.
political_impact.source: Report of the Forester, FY1908, p. 413

legacy.text: The Lincoln National Forest endures in south-central New Mexico, its boundaries adjusted many times since 1908.

today.name: Lincoln National Forest
today.note: This proclamation reduced the forest; it did not create it.

related.note: Changed the boundary of the Lincoln Forest Reserve established in 1902.
The proclamation's recital names the April 24, 1907 proclamation as the one it modifies, though that order only enlarged the forest.

later_actions.text: Wilson cut the forest again; a newspaper report put the cut near 28,000 acres, and the General Land Office restored about 15,950 acres of public land within it.
later_actions.source: Proclamation 1474, 40 Stat. 1832; Land Service Bulletin, vol. 2 (1918)

later_actions.text: Coolidge cut the forest again under the same title.

uncertain: The acreages sometimes given for the 1918 and 1924 cuts (27,784 and 19,678 acres) rest on a single compiler and have not been checked against the diagrams annexed to those proclamations.

legacy.text: The Puerta de Tierra strip the proclamation released is now dense city.

The wireless-station parcel the Navy kept was the site of Navy Radio San Juan, opened in December 1903 as the island's first wireless station; its operations later moved to Cayey, Isla Grande and Fort Allen, and the successor command was disestablished in 2004.

related.note: Conveyed to Puerto Rico most of the eighty-acre Caguas road tract reserved for the Navy in 1903.
The 1903 Marine Hospital Service reservation near San Antonio bridge, very likely the proposed Marine Hospital site the proclamation names.

uncertain: What became of each of the six San Juan parcels the Navy kept has not been traced.

reception.text: Wire services covered the October 19 drawing as a land-rush spectacle.

political_impact.text: 114,769 people registered for roughly 5,300 quarter-section claims, with 80,635 envelopes received at Dallas and 34,134 at Gregory.
political_impact.source: Santa Fe New Mexican, October 19, 1908; Sisseton Weekly Standard, October 23, 1908

political_impact.text: O'Neill, Nebraska, where 45,808 affidavits were sworn, was the busiest of the six registration towns, followed by Chamberlain with 20,248.
The Interior Department announced 838,000 acres and 5,300 farms, figures that do not match; within weeks the General Land Office commissioner said the number of quarter sections could not be given.
political_impact.source: Kingsbury County Independent, September 4, 1908; Lewiston Evening Teller, September 15, 1908

political_impact.text: There was no organized opposition beyond the affected Sicangu (Brulé) Lakota, whose objections carried little weight in the policy of the day.

legacy.text: The 1904, 1907 and 1910 openings left the reservation a checkerboard of tribal, allotted and fee land; the Supreme Court held in 1977 that the acts diminished the reservation's boundaries, over a dissent by three justices.
legacy.source: Rosebud Sioux Tribe v. Kneip, 430 U.S. 584 (1977)

related.note: The 1904 opening of the Gregory County tract of the Rosebud Reservation.

later_actions.text: The Supreme Court held that the 1907 act detached Tripp and Lyman counties from the Rosebud Sioux Reservation.
later_actions.source: Rosebud Sioux Tribe v. Kneip, 430 U.S. 584 (1977)

legacy.text: The annual observance was later fixed by law to the fourth Thursday of November.
